name: domain-industry-enricher
what_it_holds: Small DIY tool that enriches a list of top domains with industry/category classification using the Cloudflare Radar API (categorizes domains, e.g. travel, e-commerce). No committed dataset, requires a Cloudflare API token.
why_useful: Illustrates a working Cloudflare Radar API client pattern (auth, endpoint calls) that could be repointed at Radar's `/radar/ranking/top` or per-domain rank endpoints for airbnb.com and travel-sector peers; most other Cloudflare Radar repos found were internet-outage/security dashboards, not domain-rank tools.
themes: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
why_all: Illustrates a working Cloudflare Radar API client pattern (auth, endpoint calls) that could be repointed at Radar's `/radar/ranking/top` or per-domain rank endpoints for airbnb.com and travel-sector peers; most other Cloudflare Radar repos found were internet-outage/security dashboards, not domain-rank tools.

Could be paired with the cloudflare-radar-rankings-cache top-domain lists to isolate travel/OTA-category domains and track their tier membership over time as a competitor-visibility proxy, but is purely a small utility script with no data of its own.

name: cloudflare-radar (isthiam)
what_it_holds: 'Empirical analysis of global internet security across 252 countries using Cloudflare Radar API data from 2025-2026' — implies pulled and possibly committed country-level Radar metrics (traffic/security) for a broad country set, plus analysis code.
why_useful: If the underlying tables include Radar's bot-traffic-share or per-country internet-traffic-volume series (Radar publishes both), this could feed gap #19 (AI-referral / bot-traffic share) rather than domain rank specifically — worth a follow-up look at the actual files, which we did not open.
size_hint: unknown, described as 252 countries x 53 weeks x 11 studies
themes: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
why_all: If the underlying tables include Radar's bot-traffic-share or per-country internet-traffic-volume series (Radar publishes both), this could feed gap #19 (AI-referral / bot-traffic share) rather than domain rank specifically — worth a follow-up look at the actual files, which we did not open.

If country-level traffic/attack data is committed rather than just pulled live, it gives a recent (2025-2026) point-in-time snapshot of internet activity by country that could proxy regional online travel-shopping intensity (gap #5) alongside FX/consumer-strength splits (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC).

name: CloudflareRadarKit
what_it_holds: Typed Swift client library wrapping the Cloudflare Radar API (internet traffic volume, outage, BGP, and related network metrics) for iOS 17+/macOS 14+. No committed dataset — a one-call API client for pulling Cloudflare Radar's public traffic/ranking endpoints (Cloudflare also publishes a domain popularity ranking via Radar).
why_useful: Cloudflare Radar exposes a domain-ranking endpoint and traffic-share time series that could stand in for web-engagement proxies (gap #5) and AI-crawler/bot traffic share (gap #19); this client shows the API is free and scriptable even though the client itself is Swift (a Python client would need to be written against the same public endpoints).
time_coverage: live API, historical ranges depend on Radar API
themes: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
wildcard: a hedge-fund alternative-data buyer who has seen every vendo
why_all: Cloudflare Radar exposes a domain-ranking endpoint and traffic-share time series that could stand in for web-engagement proxies (gap #5) and AI-crawler/bot traffic share (gap #19); this client shows the API is free and scriptable even though the client itself is Swift (a Python client would need to be written against the same public endpoints).
Same Cloudflare Radar data source as bgpkit/radar-rs, in Swift; listed for completeness since it's a different language ecosystem — do not build both, pick one client.

name: mcp-cloudflare-radar
what_it_holds: An MCP (model-context-protocol) server wrapping Cloudflare Radar's API for traffic, attack (DDoS), BGP routing, and internet-quality metrics — a thin API bridge, not a stored dataset.
why_useful: Another confirmation the Radar API is queryable for domain/traffic-share data feeding gap #5/#19; low incremental value beyond showing endpoint coverage (traffic, BGP, quality).
